zebralogic.title: Consolidate Direct Equivalences
zebralogic.principle: Merge directly equated attribute values into a single fact and propagate it throughout the puzzle; without this, the solver may assign the two values to different houses, creating contradictions.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue contains an explicit equality between two attribute values.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'milk = gray hair' as separate constraints and placing milk in house 4 while putting gray hair in house 5.

zebralogic.title: Assign Fixed Positions Immediately
zebralogic.principle: Place any attribute that a clue pins to a specific house number (and any directly linked attributes) right away; without this, the solver may postpone placement and later encounter impossible combinations.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a house index (e.g., 'the milk drinker is in the fourth house').
zebralogic.example: Leaving the milk drinker unassigned despite the clue that it is in house 4, later causing a conflict.

zebralogic.title: Translate 'N houses between' to Exact Distance
zebralogic.principle: Convert a clue stating that exactly N houses lie between two items into a distance of N+1 houses between their positions; without this, the solver may treat the clue as a vague ordering and miss the precise spacing.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue says 'there is one house between X and Y' or similar.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting 'one house between May birthday and Peter' as simply 'May is left of Peter' and allowing them to be adjacent.

zebralogic.title: Enforce Adjacency for 'next to' and Ordered Left
zebralogic.principle: Translate adjacency clues ('next to', 'directly left of', 'directly right of') into an exact distance‑1 relationship with the correct direction; without this, the solver may place the items with a gap or in the wrong order.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses adjacency language between two attributes.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting 'auburn hair is directly left of Eric' as auburn being anywhere left of Eric, allowing a house gap.

zebralogic.title: Output Solution in Expected JSON Table Format
zebralogic.principle: Produce the final answer as a JSON object with a 'header' array listing column names and a 'rows' array of house entries; without this, the verifier cannot parse the answer.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: At the very end of the response, after all reasoning.
zebralogic.example: Returning a plain‑text table instead of the required JSON structure.

zebralogic.title: Keep Reasoning Concise to Avoid Token Truncation
zebralogic.principle: Limit explanatory text before the final JSON so the total output stays within the model's token limit; without this, the answer may be cut off and the JSON become incomplete.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: During the reasoning phase, before emitting the final answer.
zebralogic.example: Writing a long paragraph of deductions that exceeds the token budget, causing the JSON to be omitted.

zebralogic.title: Preserve Original Attribute Tokens (Case and Spelling)
zebralogic.principle: Copy attribute values verbatim from the problem statement, preserving exact case, spacing, and punctuation; without this, the verifier will treat mismatched tokens as incorrect.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When writing the final JSON rows.
zebralogic.example: Writing 'Milk' instead of 'milk' or adding extra spaces.

zebralogic.title: Directional Ordering for 'somewhere to the left/right of' constraints
zebralogic.principle: Translate clues that state 'X is somewhere to the left/right of Y' into a strict ordering constraint (X must be in a lower/higher house number than Y); without this, the solver may place X and Y in the same house or reverse the order.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses 'somewhere to the left/right of' language.
zebralogic.example: Allowing the tea drinker and the auburn‑hair person to occupy the same house despite the clue that tea is left of auburn.

zebralogic.title: Enforce Exclusion Constraints for Specific House Numbers
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states that an attribute cannot occupy a particular house, eliminate that house from its possible positions; without this, the solver may assign the attribute to the forbidden house, violating the clue.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions 'not in house X' or similar exclusion.
zebralogic.example: Placing the September birthday in house 6 despite the clue that it is not in the sixth house.

zebralogic.title: Transitive Ordering Inference
zebralogic.principle: After establishing direct left/right relationships, propagate them transitively to infer indirect orderings (e.g., if A left of B and B left of C, then A left of C); without this, the solver may miss constraints that further narrow positions.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When multiple ordering constraints share a common element, allowing a chain of orderings.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'tea left of auburn' and 'auburn left of Eric' as independent and not deducing that tea must also be left of Eric.

zebralogic.description: Generating overly long reasoning before the final answer, causing token truncation.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model tries to be thorough and does not account for the fixed token budget.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Limit reasoning to essential deductions and emit the JSON as early as possible within the token budget.

zebralogic.description: Providing the solution in a format not recognized by the verifier.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model is unaware of the exact expected output format.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Always use the prescribed JSON structure with 'header' and 'rows' fields.

zebralogic.description: Using incorrect case or synonyms for attribute values.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats attribute values as free text rather than fixed tokens.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy attribute strings verbatim from the problem statement.

zebralogic.description: Misinterpreting adjacency constraints that involve a named entity and a non‑name attribute, treating them as non‑adjacent or placing both in the same house.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model conflates adjacency with ordering and does not enforce distance‑1.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue says 'directly left of' or 'right of', enforce a distance of exactly one house.
